correctness.rationale: Every nontrivial binary Lyndon factor starts with 0 and ends 1. For n>=2 with U=C_{n-1}=V0^gV, central new gap of G=3g zeros, any crossing Lyndon factor cannot begin in left U (new gap makes later proper suffix smaller); it must be 0^t u for u prefix of U ending 1. If t>g, the leading maximal zero run makes every proper suffix lexicographically larger, so new Lyndon factor; t<=g produces an already present word if u stays in first V, otherwise an internal 0^g suffix is strictly smaller. Distinct t and ending-one prefixes yield exactly 4*6^(n-2) new words; summing yields exact all-rank formula and ternary-digit length strata. Independently constructed all substrings, direct proper-suffix Lyndon test and exact set differences for ranks 0..5: counts 1,3,7,31,175,1039. Induction rather than bounded test proves all n.
residual_risks: Only distinct linear factors, not Lyndon occurrence multiplicities or reversed binary alphabet.
